Hi Carlos —

Thanks for taking this on. As we prepare the private (air-gapped) deployment for Helios, we want to align on networking handoff points and the image signing/verification workflow so your compliance team can sign off ahead of the dry-run. Please see a short list of questions and requests below: 

- Can you confirm the final network segmentation for the isolated rack (management VLAN, data VLAN, staging VLAN) and provide a minimal topology export (subnets + jump host IPs)? We referenced an initial export attached (Helios-Network-Export-20270314.pdf).
- For offline image delivery, who will be the physical custodian at the Helios site? We need a named custodian for the chain-of-custody manifest.
- Do you require that Redwood’s signing root be kept in a customer-side HSM, or is an HSM-backed signing service run by Redwood acceptable with a publishable verification root?
- Rotation policy: what is Helios’s required maximum age for release signing keys (we typically recommend <= 90 days for release signing keys, root in HSM with 3‑person quorum for emergency signing).
- Rollback & verification: need a list of on-site commands/checks you want in the acceptance checklist (we’ll propose a default set in a follow-up from Rishi).

Next steps: if you can share the topology + preferred custodian name by EOD Tue (local), we’ll circulate Redwood’s offline signing spec and a proposed dry‑run window for the week of Mar 22.

Attachments: Helios-Network-Export-20270314.pdf (topology export)

Thanks —

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is the current topology export (helios-topology-v1.pdf). A few notes from our side:

- Segmentation: management VLAN 10.10.0.0/24 (jump host + admin), staging 10.20.0.0/24 (pre-prod verification), compute/data 10.30.0.0/22. Physical jump host will be in the locked operations room; access controlled by site badges and 2FA.
- Custodian: Anita Rao (Head of Infrastructure) will be the local custodian for receiving signed media and will sign the chain-of-custody manifest at handoff.
- HSM requirement: Helios policy prefers customer‑managed HSM for root signing keys. If Redwood keeps an HSM-backed signing service, we require a published verification root and an encrypted transfer mechanism for release signing keys prior to deployment.
- Rotation: our compliance baseline is 180 days for intermediate signing keys; root keys must be rotated on a multi-year cadence but require an on‑site verification at rotation time.

We’d like to review Redwood’s detailed offline signing procedure and the verification checklist you’ll run on-site before we schedule the dry-run.

Attachments: helios-topology-v1.pdf

Best,
Carlos

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Offline tenant networking & signing key workflow for Helios private deployment

Folks —

I put together a pragmatic offline signing & verification checklist tailored to Helios’s constraints (customer‑managed HSM preference noted). Summary below; full spec attached (redwood-offline-signing-spec-v2.pdf) and a short rollback simulation runbook (rollback-sim-runbook.md).

Key assumptions:
- Build artifacts (signed images + artifacts manifest) are produced in Redwood CI and provisioned to an encrypted transfer medium (FIPS‑validated drive or signed TAR with SHA-512 manifest).
- Root key held in customer HSM. Release signing keys are generated per-release; private release key material can be temporarily escrowed in a sealed Redwood HSM for transfer, or generated on-site using a remote attestation flow if Helios wants local key generation.
- All signed artifacts include: image checksum (SHA-512), signature block (PKCS#7), and a signed manifest signed by the release key. Manifest schema defined in spec.

Offline signing & verification flow (high level):
1) Redwood CI builds release -> produces artifacts + checksums -> creates manifest.
2) Release signing: either remote signing (Redwood HSM) OR customer-side signing via provided CSR workflow. For remote signing with customer root, we provide a verification root and perform an encrypted key transfer: ephemeral signing key wrapped with customer KMS public key.
3) Media staging: artifacts written to FIPS drive + double checksum, manifest printed and signed by custodian at Redwood.
4) Physical handoff: courier + custodian signature (Anita Rao) + chain-of-custody form. Photographic timestamp captured (optional per Helios policy).
5) On-site verification: 
   - Validate checksums: shasum -a 512 -c manifest.sha512
   - Verify signature: openssl cms -verify -in artifact.sig -inform DER -content artifact.tar.gz -CAfile verification_root.pem
   - Verify manifest matches expected release id + build id.
6) Acceptance tests: boot single node with signed image in staging VLAN, run smoke tests (container health, model load, latency check).
7) Canary/Full rollout: after passing staging, schedule rolling upgrade on compute VLAN with monitoring hooks and a 30‑min rollback window between batches.

Rollback simulation notes:
- Runbook covers a simulated rollback where a bad image is detected in staging: steps include marking release revoked in local manifest, running recovery image from staging snapshot, and updating manifests in the local artifact store. The attached runbook has commands and expected outputs for each step.

Security controls & recommendations:
- Prefer customer HSM for root; allow Redwood to generate ephemeral release keys under customer KMS wrap for transfer.
- Maintain an auditable signed manifest and an immutable artifact store (WORM/append-only) on-site.
- Key rotation: intermediate signing keys <= 90 days (recommended) given threat model; Helios stated 180 days acceptable — propose we keep release keys at 90 days and root at customer cadence, document justification for discrepancy in the compliance packet.
- Emergency signing: require 3-person quorum (Redwood ops lead, Helios custodian, Helios security lead) and on-site witness for any root operations.

I attached the full spec and the rollback simulation. If Helios wants all signing to be customer-local, we can provide the CSR and bootstrapping instructions for on-site key generation.

Attachments: redwood-offline-signing-spec-v2.pdf, rollback-sim-runbook.md

- Rishi
